threads.title: PR #1490 Add prorated credit for mid-period cancellation (Aisha)

exchanges.author: c_aisha
exchanges.subject: Review requested: #1490
exchanges.body:
Adds billing/proration.py and tests for the cancellation credit. Could you review?

```diff
+++ billing/proration.py
+"""Credit for a mid-period cancellation."""
+from datetime import date
+from decimal import ROUND_HALF_UP, Decimal
+
+
+def prorated_credit(price: str, period_start: date, period_end: date, cancel_on: date) -> Decimal:
+    days = (period_end - period_start).days + 1
+    remaining = (period_end - cancel_on).days
+    return (Decimal(price) * remaining / days).quantize(Decimal("0.01"), ROUND_HALF_UP)
+++ tests/test_proration.py
+    def test_mid_month(self):
+        self.assertEqual(prorated_credit("499.00", date(2026, 11, 1), date(2026, 11, 30), date(2026, 11, 18)),
+                         Decimal("199.60"))
+
+    def test_cancel_on_first_day(self):
+        self.assertEqual(prorated_credit("300.00", date(2026, 11, 1), date(2026, 11, 30), date(2026, 11, 1)),
+                         Decimal("290.00"))
```
CI: green.

threads.title: PR #1494 Fix reminder send time across DST changes (Jordan)

exchanges.author: worker
exchanges.body:
PR #1494 Fix reminder send time across DST changes (SUP-8812)

send_time_utc() used the tenant's current UTC offset; reminders scheduled before a DST change for a date after it were off by an hour. Now builds the aware local datetime with ZoneInfo and converts to UTC. New tests: Chicago (US fall back), London (EU fall back) and Sydney (spring forward), plus Phoenix (no DST); 3 of the 4 fail on main. Stored send_at_utc values are not fixed by this; backfill to follow under a CHG. @marcus could you review?

threads.title: SUP-8812 Reminders arriving an hour early

exchanges.author: c_gabe
exchanges.subject: Reminders arriving an hour early
exchanges.body: Three tenants (Larkfield Supply and Ostrander Labs in Chicago, Brennanvale Dental in Denver) say this morning's payment reminders went out at 8:00 local instead of 9:00. One customer called Larkfield at 8:05 annoyed. Can Billing take a look? Gabe

exchanges.author: worker
exchanges.body: Found it: send_time_utc() converts 09:00 local to UTC using the tenant's offset at the moment the reminder is scheduled, not the offset on the reminder date. Reminders scheduled before Sunday's DST change for dates after it are an hour early (08:00 CST). Fix coming today; reminders already scheduled need a backfill, which I'll plan with Tomasz. Please tell the tenants we've found the cause and are fixing it.

import unittest
from datetime import date, datetime, timezone

from billing.reminders import send_time_utc


class TestReminderDST(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_scheduled_before_us_fall_back(self):
        now = datetime(2026, 10, 30, 12, 0, tzinfo=timezone.utc)
        self.assertEqual(send_time_utc(date(2026, 11, 2), "America/Chicago", now),
                         datetime(2026, 11, 2, 15, 0, tzinfo=timezone.utc))

    def test_scheduled_before_eu_fall_back(self):
        now = datetime(2026, 10, 23, 12, 0, tzinfo=timezone.utc)
        self.assertEqual(send_time_utc(date(2026, 10, 26), "Europe/London", now),
                         datetime(2026, 10, 26, 9, 0, tzinfo=timezone.utc))

    def test_scheduled_before_sydney_spring_forward(self):
        now = datetime(2026, 10, 2, 12, 0, tzinfo=timezone.utc)
        self.assertEqual(send_time_utc(date(2026, 10, 5), "Australia/Sydney", now),
                         datetime(2026, 10, 4, 22, 0, tzinfo=timezone.utc))

    def test_phoenix_no_dst(self):
        now = datetime(2026, 10, 30, 12, 0, tzinfo=timezone.utc)
        self.assertEqual(send_time_utc(date(2026, 11, 2), "America/Phoenix", now),
                         datetime(2026, 11, 2, 16, 0, tzinfo=timezone.utc))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()
